message: Review complete: 5 finding(s) across 2 selected item(s).

comments.content: The earlier candidate's `open` throws before its database exists, so replacing it only tests removal of a stale registry entry. The database-name assertion would still pass if same-session database deletion were removed entirely. Add a replacement of a successfully created Restore candidate from the same instance, and assert that its database and registry entry are removed while the replacement remains.

const first = await p.createRestoreCandidate();
    if (first.kind === 'RuntimeNotWritable') throw new Error('not writable');

comments.content: Do not delete the candidate when `existing === candidate`. Calling activation twice (or concurrently with the same candidate) takes this branch after the first call installs the pointer, deleting the active Workspace while leaving the pointer intact. If a Workspace connection is open, deletion also triggers its versionchange handler. Guard the deletion with an identity check and add a repeated-activation test.

Same-instance preparations are not serialized across the read/delete/list/create sequence. Two concurrent `createRestoreCandidate()` calls can both read an empty earlier list, then each append and create a database, leaving two Restore candidates for the same session instead of replacing the earlier one. Serialize the complete preparation operation per instance and cover overlapping calls in a test.

The new Restore metadata is still erased by `createCandidate()`, which overwrites the candidates record with only `key` and `databaseNames`. For example, `createRestoreCandidate(); createCandidate(); createRestoreCandidate()` leaves the first Restore database behind because its session entry is lost. Update the migration-candidate append path to preserve `restoreCandidates` as well, and test mixed candidate creation.

Also refuse when this persistence instance is superseded. The Workspace `versionchange` handler sets the local `superseded` flag without updating the injected write gate, so `current()` can still return null after another tab replaces the Workspace. Unlike `commit()`, this method then creates and lists a Restore database for a session that must no longer write. Apply the superseded refusal logic before any root/database operations, and cover a versionchange with an otherwise-writable gate.
